newsitem.title: USA: TALKING POINT - Safeway, Vons deal.
newsitem.headline: TALKING POINT - Safeway, Vons deal.

text.p: Safeway Inc's proposed takeover of Vons Cos Inc is not expected to run into serious opposition from Vons, but industry experts Wednesday said Safeway may have to increase its offer slightly.

Safeway, which already owns 34.5 percent of Vons, announced an offer to acquire the remaining shares in a stock swap that values Vons at around $58 a share, a hefty premium from Tuesday's closing price of 43-1/8.
Vons, which operates 325 stores in Southern California, said it is studying the offer and will respond in due course.
Industry analysts said Safeway's proposal appeared to be fair. But they said the giant supermarket chain may need to increase the stock ratio to complete the transaction.

"My sense is that they'll get it done, but possibly at a slightly higher ratio," said Steven Cohen, head of research for Kellner DiLeo and Co. "Since Safeway owns so much of Vons, they'll have to raise it to look like they negotiated on behalf of the shares not held by Safeway."
Under terms of the proposed merger, Vons shareholders would receive 1.34 Safeway shares for each Vons shares. Vons has about 44 million shares outstanding.
In a conference call with analysts and reporters, Safeway Chief Executive Steve Burd said it was too early to speculate on whether Safeway would sweeten the deal.
"We've made a full and fair offer right from the opening bell," he said, adding the company has given Vons two weeks to respond.
Analysts said the combination of Safeway and Vons would create a supermarket powerhouse with 1,375 stores in 16 states, the District of Columbia and parts of Canada.

"The combination will make for a western USA powerhouse without equal. It's very exciting for Safeway holders in in the longer term and its a fair price, " said Mark Husson, analyst with J.P. Morgan Securities.
In a brief statement, Vons said its review would be conducted by a commitee of outside directors.
Safeway has several members on Vons' board.
Kohlberg Kravis Roberts, which owns 52 percent of Safeway's shares and has representatives on its board, said it approved of the transaction.
"Safeway's management approached the board and we approved it," a spokesman said.
Safeway shares were off 1-3/4 to 41-5/8 while Vons was up 10-1/4 to 53-3/8.
